All can enjoy, a free meal.
They need 2) a ticket 3) a pass.

direction_summaries.explanation: This feature lights up on tokens that kick off new syntactic chunks—especially nominal or prepositional phrases and clause-initial markers.  In practice it activates on prepositions (of, by, in), the determiner “the,” their head nouns (mechanism, predator, conductivity, concentrations, project), and clause-openers (All, It’s), signalling PP attachments and phrase boundaries in both technical and everyday text.

direction_summaries.explanation: This feature fires on tokens that act as structural or formatting markers across different text genres—things like delimiters (parentheses, braces, quotes, asterisks), metadata labels or section flags (“mode”, “Pag” in a paginator), citation markers (“((g))”, footnote “*”), and similar keywords (“future”, “mathematics” as topical headers). In other words, it detects the typographic and keyword cues that outline document structure, metadata, or formatting placeholders in code, legal citations, and technical prose.
